translation: By her form she pervades the universe and stands established.
Likewise abiding in the body, she awakens embodied beings by means of śakti.

sanskrit: taṃ cādau śrūyatāṃ samyakta tatvato tu krameṇa tu ||
translation: And let that be heard at the outset, rightly, in accordance with reality — and in due sequence.

sanskrit: piṃḍaṃ padaṃ tathā rūpaṃ rūpāpātītaṃ caturthakam ||
translation: The piṇḍa, the pada, likewise the form, and the fourth, which transcends the manifestation of form.

sanskrit: piṃḍasthaṃ tu caturdhā vai mukhyato varavarṇiniḥ ||
translation: The one abiding in the piṇḍa is fourfold, indeed, chiefly, O excellent-complexioned one.
Abiding in the piṇḍa, abiding in all piṇḍas, established while enveloping the piṇḍa.

sanskrit: pātālamūcakraṃ tu carākhye tu dvidhā sthitam ||
translation: The cakra at the root of the pātāla — in the one called carā — is established as twofold.
Thus, in the same way … (lacuna) … in a moment.
Made into a single piṇḍa — everything, the all-clay piṇḍa — O good-vowed one.

sanskrit: māraye tṛdaśātasmiṃ manuje naiva kā kathā ||
translation: If it can kill even the thirty gods, what need to speak of a man?

sanskrit: yakṣiṇī sādhanaṃ tava śatajit prathame pade ||
translation: The yakṣiṇī sādhana is yours, O Śatajit, in the first pāda.
The fourth — and the fourth(?) — beginning with the pādukā, bestowing renown.

sanskrit: tatra prāṇa śataiḥ paṃcaikāmadeva samo bhavet ||
translation: There, with a hundred prāṇas, one would become equal to the Pañcaikāmadeva(?).
This(?) — of the one above … (lacuna) … afflicted by desire. [corrupt]
Women seize by force even an unwilling lord of heroes.
It is accomplished together with the piṇḍa, through the power of Kāmarāja.
Therefore it is called 'Kāma'; now hear (about) the yoni-born.
The revolving circle and the whirl — the body is indeed possessed (by them).
The mind abiding in the supreme state would lead, being drawn(?), to non-mind.
He makes graceful poetry, adorned and captivating.

sanskrit: vatrāye trīṇi lokāni devāsu rasa kiṃnarāḥ ||
translation: (He wanders?) the three worlds — gods, asuras(?), seers(?), and kinnaras. [corrupt]
And he lives countless (years), conquering death and non-death, O man.
Paralysis, deluding, uprooting, subjugation, enmity, and so on.
From dhāraṇā, from union with the essence, and from the establishment of one's own form (these arise).
O five-formed great goddess, (they are) well established with forbearance(?).
Endowed with the state of being indeed, it would then bring the sixteenfold quality(?).

sanskrit: rūpādi parivartaṃ ca sthāvare jaṃgamepi vā ||
translation: And the transformation of form and the rest — in the immobile or in the mobile.
With water he would flood the whole world, immobile and mobile.

sanskrit: jalaiḥ bhūtvā vrajed devi yatrecchā yoginasya tu ||
translation: Having become water, the yogin would go wherever he wishes, O goddess.

sanskrit: tanmadhye samatāṃ yāti vahni puṃjamiva svayat ||
translation: In the midst of that he attains equality — like a mass of fire itself(?).

sanskrit: viyaṃ daśadiśaścaiva bhramate ca kṣaṇena tu ||
translation: Having abandoned the ten directions, he roams about in a moment.
The yogin becomes one whose life is his own will; from the practice of that — no doubt.
Now I shall declare another — the dvekuṃṭha(?), devoid of the hundred-thousand.
There, having made the state firm, (he has) prowess equal to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: bhogārtasthā bhuvanakte tu ante līyati sāsvate ||
translation: …at the end it dissolves into the eternal(?). [corrupt]
He perceives the mind's abode; in the mind is the contemplation of consciousness.

sanskrit: prāṇaṃ caiva sthiraṃ kṛtvā aṇimādi prasādhanam ||
translation: And having made the prāṇa steady — (this is) the accomplishment of aṇimā and the rest.
The yogin is born with a self-willed life; he would become lord of his own body.

sanskrit: tatsarvaṃ tasya pratyakṣaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
translation: All that becomes directly manifest to him — here there is no doubt.
In (the cakra) called Lolā there is no doubt; above that one becomes immortal.
The lord of sādhakas becomes endowed with splendor and fame.

sanskrit: tadā tasya mahābhāge sidhyate yogi maṃḍalam ||
translation: Then, O great-fated one, the maṇḍala is accomplished for him, O yogin.
It shakes, it trembles, and indeed it falls and springs up again.

sanskrit: caktraṃ tu paramaṃ devi nāstyatra pravicāraṇā ||
translation: The supreme cakra, O goddess — here there is no deliberation.
…(one attains) the Kaulikī speech — the binding of mudrās in many ways. [corrupt]
…the union occurs at once, O beautiful-hipped one. [corrupt]
The fourth is called the piṇḍa, beyond thought(?), O worshipped-by-heroes one.

sanskrit: ghūrmi mātraṃ bhavet tatra yadā niścalanāṃgataḥ ||
translation: There it becomes mere whirling, when it has attained stillness(?).
And flight through the sky — no doubt — arises from practice, from yoga.
Without it, neither a god nor a lord of nāgas would become a direct knower of all scriptures(?).
The division of the four piṇḍas, together with its secret, is revealed.
It is to be understood through the distinction of dissolution — immediately joined with realization.
And the manifold divisions of rites, and their number, arise.
From the essence arise the varied attainments, greatly flourishing with manifold qualities.
Thus, in the Kulasāra, the fourth chapter.
The blessed Bhairava said.
The one piṇḍa became twofold; from twofold, manifold.
(It becomes) day-and-night (of) dharma and adharma, in the form of nāda and bindu.

sanskrit: na tatra lakṣaṇo lakṣyaṃ lakṣātītaṃ niraṃjanam ||
translation: There there is no mark, no object of marking — (it is) beyond marking, stainless.
Pervading the ether, unmanifest, supreme-and-other, contemplated.
Hence, what is devoid of bliss — its illumination is what follows after it.
(It appears) like moonbeams — moonlight, through the union of consciousness.
Then he sees her who abides in the body, and the pātāla worlds likewise.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca paśya yogavit tadā ||
translation: Past, present, and future — the knower of yoga sees (them) then.
Vārās and vīreśvarās(?), siddhas, vidyādharas, together with kinnaras.
Restrained in the sky-cakra by the resounding of kettle-drum sounds…
(He is) … — going everywhere, pervading, liberated from the bonds of saṃsāra.

sanskrit: uccārya śaktiṃ śubhage uccāraṃ tasya yojanam ||
translation: Having uttered śakti, O fortunate one — (this is) its utterance and application.
For this, O womb of true knowledge, is the Kaula (teaching) that must not be revealed.
Hard to obtain by all yogins, (and) not to be spoken — thus it is proclaimed.
Thus, in the Kulasāra, the eighth chapter.
The blessed Bhairava said.
Siddhas find there the mantra-mother(?), radiant (with qualities).
(The yoginī) whose food is surrounded by consciousness-mantras… [verse corrupt]

sanskrit: na maṃtroddharaṇārthāya tasmāt sāmarthatā na hi ||
translation: Not for the sake of mantra-extraction — therefore there is indeed no capability.
The blessed Bhairava said.
The śakti-tattva, O great-fated one — the mantra dissolves (into it)(?).
In the abode of attaining that, a being (meets) no confusion, O dear one.
The (calamity of) motion-and-memory(?) is warded off by the mantra's śakti, O great goddess.
The burnt jīva — let it sprout(?) … for them, O Maheśvarī. [corrupt]
The blessed Goddess said.
For one who has entered the wrath-class(?), welfare arises from Śiva alone.
The blessed Bhairava said.
The secret that was not told to anyone, whose domain is hidden.
The reality established as directly perceptible — the all-pervading Maheśvara.
Joined with the six limbs of Śiva, they roam in the auspicious …(?). [corrupt]

sanskrit: icchayā samatāṃ yāti icchayā saṃbhavanti ca ||
translation: By will (she) attains equality; by will (they) arise.
This is omniscience — the ever-content illumination.
The quality effecting all-pervasion is the succession of the infinite śaktis.
By understanding that there is no lordship; rather, this quality is the omnipotent one's śakti.
Thus addressed, O great goddess, Śiva himself, ever(?)…
His mind absorbed in That — it is to be known as possessed of that quality(?), O dear one.

sanskrit: mukti svaśaktenantabhānārthaṃ anādi vodhāśca samantatā? ca ||
translation: Liberation — for the sake of the inner realization(?) of one's own śakti — beginningless; and understanding, and completeness(?). [corrupt]
The …(?) supreme secret, to be guarded with effort.
The blessed Goddess said.
By the grace of that, tell me, O Parameśvara, (the way to) the attainment of that.
The state of agitation and non-agitation — as I know it, well-ascertained.
With your mind fixed on That, tell (me), O lord of gods, O all-pervading Maheśvara.
The blessed Bhairava said.
Hear (about) the success that effects the attainment of that — the whole essence of reality.
